title.en: Inverted conditionals: Had I known, Should you need, Were it not for

summary.en: In formal English you can drop _if_ and put the auxiliary first. Three auxiliaries do this: **had** (third conditional), **should** (a possible future event) and **were** (unreal present). _If I had known_ becomes _**Had I known**_; _If you need help_ becomes _**Should you need** help_; _If I were you_ becomes _**Were I** you_. This is different from inversion after negative adverbials: here the trigger is a missing _if_. It is very useful in the formal email of Writing part 4 (_Should you require further details, please contact me_).
summary.es: Se quita if y el auxiliar pasa delante del sujeto: Had I known = «de haberlo sabido». Es muy formal y se usa sobre todo por escrito.

form: **Had** + subject + past participle, **would have** + past participle (= if + past perfect)
**Should** + subject + base verb, imperative / will / can (= if + present, an unlikely or polite possibility)
**Were** + subject + **to** + infinitive, **would** + infinitive (= if + past simple); **Were** + subject + adjective / noun
Negative: **not** goes after the subject: _Had I **not** left_, never _Hadn't I left_
**Had it not been for / Were it not for** + noun = _if it hadn't been for / if it weren't for_

uses.text: **Formal letters and emails**: _Should you wish to cancel, please let us know by Friday._
**Regret about the past**: _Had I realised how late it was, I would have called a taxi._
**Unreal present in careful speech or writing**: _Were I in your position, I would accept the offer._
**Saying that something depended on one factor**: _Were it not for the volunteers, the festival would not happen._

mistakes.wrong: Had I knew about the delay, I would have booked another flight.
mistakes.right: Had I known about the delay, I would have booked another flight.

why.en: Had here is the auxiliary of the past perfect, so the verb needs a past participle.
why.es: Had es el auxiliar de «hubiera»: después va el participio (known).

mistakes.wrong: Hadn't I taken the map, we would have got lost.
mistakes.right: Had I not taken the map, we would have got lost.

why.en: In inverted conditionals the negative is not contracted: not follows the subject.
why.es: No se contrae: Had I not…, nunca Hadn't I…

mistakes.wrong: Should you will need help, call me.
mistakes.right: Should you need help, please call me.

why.en: After should (= if), the verb is the base form, without will.
why.es: Tras should va el infinitivo sin to ni will.

mistakes.wrong: Was I in your position, I would think twice.
mistakes.right: Were I in your position, I would think twice.

why.en: The inverted form of the unreal present uses were for every person.
why.es: En esta estructura se usa siempre were, incluso con I.

examples.en: Had I known about the strike, I would have driven to work.
Had the train been on time, we would have made the meeting.
examples.es: Si el tren hubiera llegado a su hora, habríamos llegado a la reunión.

examples.en: Had she not accepted the offer, she would still be unemployed.
Should you require further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
examples.es: Si necesita más información, no dude en ponerse en contacto con nosotros.

examples.en: Should the weather turn bad, the ceremony will be held indoors.
Were I in your position, I would think twice before signing.
Were the company to move abroad, hundreds of jobs would be lost.
Were it not for her experience, the project would be in serious trouble.
examples.es: Si no fuera por su experiencia, el proyecto estaría en serios apuros.

examples.en: Had it not been for the rain, we would have had a perfect weekend.
Should you change your mind, the offer will remain open until May.

practice.prompt: ___ the train been on time, we would have made the meeting.

explanation.en: Had + subject + past participle replaces if the train had been on time.

practice.prompt: ___ you need any further information, please contact our office.

explanation.en: Should + subject + base verb is the formal way to say if you need.

practice.prompt: Had I ___ about the strike, I would have driven instead.

explanation.en: Had needs a past participle: known.

practice.prompt: Had it ___ for the rain, we would have had a perfect weekend.

explanation.en: The fixed pattern is Had it not been for + noun.

practice.prompt: ___ I in your position, I would think twice before signing.

explanation.en: The inverted unreal present uses were.
